Set the temperature of the *Sea* (24 to 31 °C) and follow the maximum wind and the category on the right; a day counter runs at the top (one second is three hours). *Landfall* pushes the storm onto the land, *Restart* brings it back over the sea, and *North* and *South* choose the hemisphere.

::: {.column-page}
{{< geores sim="hurricane" >}}
:::

## What to look for

- Below which sea temperature does the storm die?
- Set the sea to 27, 29 and 31 °C in turn: which category does the storm reach each time?
- How many days does the storm take to reach its strongest wind? How long does it take to weaken after *Landfall*?
- Why does the storm weaken over land, even when the land is hot?
- Which way does the storm turn in the northern hemisphere? In the southern hemisphere?

## How it works

The maximum wind moves towards a target set by the sea temperature alone: only a weak depression below 26.5 °C, then a stronger storm the warmer the sea, up to 300 km/h. Over land the target is zero, and the wind dies down within about a day. The category follows the Saffir-Simpson thresholds in km/h. Real cyclones also depend on other conditions, such as the winds higher up and the humidity of the air, which the model leaves out.
